challenges.says: The criterion for businessrule-25371901799273876158 drops the rule's condition that a start-up load also discards the workspace.

The criterion that a policy option of an unknown kind is dropped without notice cites only the legacy rule, yet base.decision-16 says an unknown policy element is kept and reported, never silently dropped; the contradiction is neither resolved nor cited.
The criterion that any other control is dropped without notice conflicts with base.decision-16 (unknown elements are kept and reported) and neither cites nor reconciles it.

The criteria on an imported registry source restate rules that describe the live registry, but they do not cite integrations.decision-2 that turns the live registry into imported files, so the builder cannot see why the rule applies to imports.

The story joins two unrelated rules, and its wording (an 'XML attribute' returning nothing, 'server rendered', 'decisions make the service...') is not something a product owner who never saw the code could follow.
